protocol.instrument_name: NCCTRC Pharmacist Immunisation Scheduled Substance Treatment Protocol (SSTP) (cover title: National Critical Care and Trauma Centre - Additional Pharmacist Vaccinations SSTP)
protocol.instrument_version: No version number printed; Schedule A publication date 10 March 2026; Chief Health Officer approval dated 31/03/2026 (EDOC2026/69995)
protocol.legal_basis: Medicines, Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 2012 (NT): Chief Health Officer approves the protocol 'under section 254(1) of the Act' and states each protocol 'remains in effect for a period of 2 years on and from the date of this instrument' under 'section 254(3) of the Act' (p.1, Approval). Period of effect: 'This SSTP remains in effect until 31/03/2028 unless revoked earlier.' (p.5).
protocol.supervision_model: SSTP-authorised pharmacist model, document terminology: 'Health Professionals authorised by this SSTP: Pharmacists employed by or contracted to the National Critical Care and Trauma Response Centre' (p.3). No supervising practitioner is printed; the boundary of the authorisation is stated on p.6: 'If contraindications or exclusions are present, health professionals must refer the matter to an authorised prescriber for an administration order.' Accreditation requirements (p.4-5): Pharmacy Board registration with no conditions or undertakings limiting clinical services, an approved immunisation training certificate, maintained CPD and a current CPR certificate.
protocol.scope_summary: Scheduled Substance Treatment Protocol (SSTP) authorising pharmacists employed by or contracted to the National Critical Care and Trauma Response Centre to administer Cholera, Rabies and Typhoid vaccines to persons aged 5 years and over, NT wide. Doses, dose frequency, contraindications and interactions are deferred to the current version of the Australian Immunisation Handbook. Prints screening/consent duties, anaphylaxis preparedness requirements (second person with Basic Life Support or Provide First Aid certificate; complete Emergency Response Kit contents), premises requirements, 15-minute post-vaccination monitoring, adverse event reporting to the NT Centre for Disease Control, accreditation requirements and Australian Immunisation Register documentation duties.

inclusion.text: Health Professionals authorised by this SSTP: Pharmacists employed by or contracted to the National Critical Care and Trauma Response Centre

provenance.section_heading: Health Professionals authorised by this SSTP

inclusion.text: Indication: All persons aged 5 years and over as per Australian Immunisation Handbook
Scheduled Substance(s) within scope: Cholera Vaccine; Rabies Vaccine; Typhoid Vaccine
Be registered with the Pharmacy Board of Australia with no conditions or undertakings which may limit delivery of clinical services directly to patients

Hold a current certificate of completion of either: Prior to 1 January 2017: APPIMM806A - Manage the delivery and administration of injections and immunisations -Pharmaceutical Society of Australia; or 10455NAT - Course in conduct immunisation services within a community pharmacy environment - Pharmacy Guild of Australia; After 1 January 2017: a training program accredited as meeting the standards set by the Australian Pharmacy Council's 'Standards for the accreditation of programs to support Pharmacist Administration of vaccines'.
Maintain continuing professional development related to skills and competencies required for the delivery of medicines and vaccines including the use of multi-dose vials and management of anaphylaxis
Hold a current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) certificate

exclusion.text: Contraindications and/or Exclusions: As per the current Australian Immunisation Handbook
Where the Australian Immunisation Handbook states vaccination is not recommended for specific cohorts, such as pregnant women or immunocompromised patients, this protocol cannot be used in that group
Pharmacists may only administer vaccines to patients aged 5 years and above
If contraindications or exclusions are present, health professionals must refer the matter to an authorised prescriber for an administration order.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Vaccination suitability, administration and follow-up (NCCTRC SSTP)

steps.description: 'Immunisation providers should screen people for eligibility before vaccination, obtain valid consent, and ensure that the correct equipment and procedures are in place before vaccination.' Eligibility is per the Indication (all persons aged 5 years and over as per Australian Immunisation Handbook) and the current Australian Immunisation Handbook.

gates.criterion: Person screened for eligibility before vaccination (aged 5 years and over, per the current Australian Immunisation Handbook)

steps.description: If contraindications or exclusions are present, refer: 'health professionals must refer the matter to an authorised prescriber for an administration order.'

Obtain valid consent before vaccination: 'Immunisation providers should screen people for eligibility before vaccination, obtain valid consent, and ensure that the correct equipment and procedures are in place before vaccination.' Patient consent (written or verbal) for vaccination must be recorded and records of consent maintained by the clinical service (p.5, Documentation).

gates.criterion: Valid consent obtained before vaccination and recorded

steps.description: Anaphylaxis preparedness check (Management of Anaphylaxis): 'Administration of any vaccine from this protocol must occur where another person, who holds a current Basic Life Support Certificate or Provide First Aid Certificate, is immediately available to provide emergency assistance if required' AND 'must occur where there is a complete anaphylaxis Emergency Response Kit ... in line with procedures from the current Australian Immunisation Handbook'. Kit must be checked regularly, maintained, easily accessible and contain: Adrenaline 1:1000 (minimum of 3 ampoules); 1mL syringes and 25mm needles for IM injection (minimum of 3 of each); Cotton wool swabs; Pen and paper to record time of administration of adrenaline; Laminated copy of 'Recognition and treatment of anaphylaxis' and the 'Doses of intramuscular 1:1000 adrenaline for anaphylaxis'.

gates.criterion: Second person with a current Basic Life Support Certificate or Provide First Aid Certificate immediately available AND complete anaphylaxis Emergency Response Kit present with printed contents

steps.description: Premises check: 'Vaccines must be administered in a location that: ensures privacy of the consumer; ensures sufficient room to accommodate the consumer, carer and immuniser and allow sufficient space, surfaces and be able to respond to medical emergencies including sufficient space for the consumer to lie down if required; has equipment to facilitate safe immunisation administration including Easy access to a sink with running water and hand soap for washing hands and/or ready access to hand sanitiser, Sharps disposal container and dedicated bin for medical waste, Equipment and storage facilities to meet the National Vaccine Storage Guidelines, Consumables for the delivery of a vaccine eg needles, hypoallergenic tape, cottonwool swabs and/or adhesive bandage strips'. 'Vaccines must be stored in accordance with the National Vaccine Storage Guidelines'.

gates.criterion: Administration location meets all printed premises, equipment, storage and privacy requirements

steps.description: Administer Cholera Vaccine, Rabies Vaccine or Typhoid Vaccine: 'Dose and Route as per the current version Australian Immunisation Handbook'. 'Dosing frequency, and intervals between vaccines, as per the current version Australian Immunisation Handbook'. 'As per interactions listed in the current Australian Immunisation Handbook and individual vaccine product information.'

'Post vaccination procedures should be followed as per the Australian Immunisation Handbook. All patients must be monitored post vaccination for 15 minutes unless they withdraw consent to be monitored. Ensure withdrawn consent is documented in the person's clinical record.'

gates.criterion: Patient monitored post vaccination for 15 minutes unless consent to be monitored is withdrawn and documented

steps.description: 'Report any adverse event during or post vaccination to the NT Centre for Disease Control using the 'Adverse event following vaccination' form available online or in hard copy on the Recording and reports on immunisations | NT Health'.

Documentation: 'Complete all clinical documentation requirements as outlined by the Health Service' and 'Enter the patient details, vaccine brand name, dose, site of administration and batch number in the Australian Immunisation Register within 24 hours, and no later than 10 days, after administration. For many vaccine providers this involves entry into routine clinical information systems for automatic upload.'

gates.criterion: Australian Immunisation Register entry made within 24 hours, and no later than 10 days, after administration

open_questions.topic: No version number printed for this SSTP
open_questions.observed: Cover page (p.1) prints title and approval (dated 31/03/2026, EDOC2026/69995); Schedule A (p.2) prints Publication Date 10 March 2026; no 'V1/V2' style version string appears anywhere.
open_questions.why_unclear: instrument_version recorded as the printed publication/approval dates because no version number exists in the document.

open_questions.topic: Printed pagination vs PDF page markers
open_questions.observed: Footers print 'Page 1 of 4' to 'Page 4 of 4' on PDF pages 3-6; PDF pages 1-2 (CHO approval and Schedule A) are unnumbered approval pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: All provenance page numbers in this file use the === PAGE n === markers (PDF pages 1-6); printed footer numbers are offset by 2.

open_questions.topic: No numeric dose, route or frequency printed
open_questions.observed: 'Dose and Route* Dose and Route as per the current version Australian Immunisation Handbook' (p.3) and 'Dose Frequency* Dosing frequency, and intervals between vaccines, as per the current version Australian Immunisation Handbook' (p.4).
open_questions.why_unclear: No dose numbers, volumes, routes or intervals can be transcribed; the authoritative dosing source (Australian Immunisation Handbook) version is not pinned in the document.

open_questions.observed: Screening, consent, 15-minute monitoring and AIR entry are stated as 'should'/'must' duties with no printed branch if not met (pp.3-5).
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not state what happens when these steps fail, so gates use on_fail 'unclear' rather than an invented branch.

open_questions.topic: Serological testing referral wording is conditional
open_questions.observed: p.2 Note: 'a referral to a medical practitioner may be required for serological testing and result interpretation to determine suitability for vaccination where stated in the Australian Immunisation Handbook'.
open_questions.why_unclear: 'may be required' defers to the Australian Immunisation Handbook; no serology list is printed in this document. Captured as referral.routine only.

open_questions.observed: Referral-related statements appear on pp.2-6 (serology note p.2; second-person emergency assistance p.3; authorised-prescriber referral p.6). No routine follow-up referral destination (e.g. GP review) is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Shared referral provenance uses the first page (3, Management of Anaphylaxis); the routine list contains only the conditional serology referral, which is hedged with 'may be required'.

open_questions.topic: Title and scope inconsistencies in the source
open_questions.observed: Cover title (p.1) is 'National Critical Care and Trauma Centre - Additional Pharmacist Vaccinations SSTP' and Schedule A (p.2) title is 'NCCTRC Pharmacist Immunisation Scheduled Substance Treatment Protocol (SSTP)', while header on pp.4-6 reads 'Immunisation Scheduled Substance Treatment Protocol (SSTP) for Pharmacists'. 'Areas Applicable' prints 'NT Wide' but authorised pharmacists must be employed by or contracted to the NCCTRC.
open_questions.why_unclear: instrument_name taken from the Schedule A title (the formally approved title); the relationship between 'NT Wide' applicability and the NCCTRC employment restriction is not explained.

open_questions.observed: Adverse event reporting is printed on p.4; Australian Immunisation Register entry on p.5.
open_questions.why_unclear: Shared notifiable provenance uses the first page (4); both conditions are quoted with their own page numbers.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pin the current version of the Australian Immunisation Handbook (and any NT Centre for Disease Control advice) that governs dose, route, frequency, intervals and contraindications for Cholera, Rabies and Typhoid vaccines before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The SSTP prints no dose itself; every dosing and contraindication rule is deferred to 'the current version' of an external document that is not version-pinned.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the pharmacist's employment or contract status with the National Critical Care and Trauma Response Centre, and reconcile 'Areas Applicable: NT Wide' (p.3) with the NCCTRC employment/contract restriction.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Authorisation is limited to NCCTRC-employed or contracted pharmacists while the areas field says NT Wide; jurisdictional scope is ambiguous.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local rostering/process so that another person holding a current Basic Life Support Certificate or Provide First Aid Certificate is immediately available whenever a vaccine from this protocol is administered, and confirm Emergency Response Kit checking schedule.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Operational precondition printed as a 'must' but no local procedure, check frequency ('checked regularly') or responsible person is specified.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the complete vaccine scope: the cover title says 'Additional Pharmacist Vaccinations' but only Cholera, Rabies and Typhoid vaccines are listed as scheduled substances (p.3).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Title implies a broader or additional vaccine list; only three substances are printed, so the authoritative scope must be confirmed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the current Australian Immunisation Handbook position on cohorts where vaccination is not recommended (e.g. pregnant women, immunocompromised patients) before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Exclusion is defined entirely by an external, version-changing document; the SSTP prints no cohort list of its own.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the local pathway for serological testing referrals to a medical practitioner ('may be required ... where stated in the Australian Immunisation Handbook', p.2), including which serologies apply for Cholera/Rabies/Typhoid vaccination decisions.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Conditional ('may be required') referral with no named practitioner, timeframe or testing list printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the Australian Immunisation Register submission mechanism and the 24-hour / 10-day entry workflow for this service.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Deadline is printed but the operational route ('routine clinical information systems for automatic upload') depends on local systems.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the premises arrangements: this SSTP prints generic location requirements (p.4) with no PS5 pharmacy-premises clause and no separate pharmacy/non-pharmacy split, unlike the NT Pharmacist Immunisation SSTP.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Premises standard applicable to the service is not stated in this document; jurisdictional/hedged detail must be confirmed locally.
